summary: Both round-5 blocking issues are resolved and neither is re-raised. Codex B_DEFINED_NONDETERMINISM is resolved by its own preferred option: deterministic soft-float in both builds, with a single canonical NaN, round-to-nearest-even, llvm.fmuladd rewritten to fmul+fadd, fast-math stripped, and hardware floating point never executed, so NaN bits, fusion and intermediate rounding agree through bitcast and branches by construction; floating point is correctly removed from the deferred list. Opus B_RESIDUAL_NONDETERMINISM is resolved on all three of its points: fmuladd and NaN by the soft-float rewrite, and addresses by a deterministic layout model with a shared allocator shim at fixed base plus opus's option A for the stack (provenance-tracked layout-dependent executions excluded from native comparison, validated against the reference interpreter, recorded in the certificate); faulting access and atomics/volatile are also now fixed, fault causes come from the interpreter, and the normaliser version is certificated. Crucially the fix closes the class, not the instances: section 3.2 states that the reference semantics fixes every remaining LLVM choice, with normative enumeration and an independently implemented validator in the dialect spec, which is the right vision-level form for residual spec work now routed to the ISA and dialect specs. Re-grading from scratch, I found no remaining false premise, contradiction or missing load-bearing piece that would make the project build the wrong thing; the residuals are one leftover contradictory phrase about region-input zero-initialisation, the unstated format/libm scope of the soft-float rewrite, and the mechanics of global layout in the native link, all recorded as suggestions. The vision is unreasonably ambitious, right, and precise enough for strangers to build from.
